overall: Tomorrow (Thursday, July 2) in Los Angeles looks like a cool, marine-influenced day with patchy morning fog clearing by 11am, followed by partly sunny skies. Southwest winds of 5–15 mph will keep coastal temperatures moderated, consistent with a typical June Gloom pattern lingering into early July. No severe weather is expected locally, though a Lake Wind Advisory is active for the West Side Mountains north of 198 and an unrelated Air Quality Alert covers Imperial County.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor and spread across a wide range. ECMWF is the coolest at ~72.0°F, GFS and WEATHER_COM cluster near 75–75.4°F, while HRRR and NBM are warmer at 78–78.8°F — a spread of roughly 7°F between the coolest and warmest guidance. The NWS official text forecast calls for a high near 68°F, which is meaningfully below all NWP model expectations and aligns more closely with prior-day observations (68°F), suggesting the NWS is leaning heavily on marine influence and fog persistence.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble expected TMAX of 72.4°F sits between the conservative NWS text forecast (68°F) and the warmer NWP guidance (75–79°F range), with probability mass spread flatly across six consecutive 2°F buckets from 66–77°F at roughly 20% each — a hallmark of genuine model uncertainty. Both the even and odd bucket sets are rated Tier 4 (Poor signals — AVOID), indicating low confidence and no dominant outcome. Best estimate is approximately 72°F, leaning slightly toward the ensemble mean and ECMWF, but the NWS call of 68°F cannot be dismissed given the fog pattern and prior-day anchor.
